newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Manuel under fire in reshuffle reports.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Manuel under fire in reshuffle reports.

text.p: South African newspaper reports that Finance Minister Trevor Manuel would be moved in a major cabinet reshuffle were on Friday described as speculation but not denied by the president's office.

Newspapers in Durban and Cape Town carried reports quoting "top African National Congress sources" as saying President Nelson Mandela would announce a reshuffle early next month and that Alec Erwin, now minister of trade and industry, was likely to replace Manuel.
The reports said Manuel would become foreign minister in place of Alfred Nzo, whose policies have frequently been criticised as lacking direction.
Manuel's spokeswoman Jennifer Wilson referred queries on the reports to Mandela's office, where they were treated with disdain.
"It's sheer speculation at this stage," Mandela's spokesman Parks Mankahlana said, without denying that a reshuffle could be on the cards.
Financial market dealers said rumours that Erwin would replace Manuel had been doing the rounds for nearly six weeks and many said they hoped the reports were true.
"There's been a feeling in the market that we needed a new finance minister ever since Manuel was appointed in April," one dealer said.
"Alec Erwin would be the right man for the job," the dealer said, adding that Erwin's communist party background did not count against him in the current climate.
Another dealer echoed the sentiment: "(Manuel) has been a political disaster, though he might have been good at his numbers."
A source close to Manuel who did not want to be identified said he held a brief conversation on Friday with the finance minister, who had dismissed the press reports.
"These things surface every now and then," the source said. "The thing that worries me is that it discredits Trevor a lot because they constantly suggest that he is not good enough at economics."
The source said that although Manuel was appointed two months after the rand began a precipitous slide in February last year, market players firmly linked him to the currency's continued weakness.
The rand has lost about 30 percent of its value since mid- February and was trading at around 4.70 to the dollar on Friday.

Economic analysts say investor confidence in the economy can be resurrected only through concrete steps to implement the growth policies which Manuel outlined in June last year to general approval from business.
ANC sources said speculation was rife within the party over an imminent reshuffle, with Defence Minister Joe Modise frequently mentioned as likely to step down soon due to ill health.
One ANC source said: "There is a perception that Manuel has to go. Not that he has been a disaster but he's not seen as quite up to the job."
